{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This file is autogenerated by maturin v1.7.0
# To update, run
#
#    maturin generate-ci github
#
name: CI

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - '*'
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  linux:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform.runner }}

    strategy:
      matrix:
        platform:
          - runner: ubuntu-22.04
            target: x86_64
   
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '>=3.10'  # Choose the Python version you need
          
      - name: Install Maturin
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install maturin[patchelf]
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
          sudo apt update
          sudo apt install -y libssl-dev  # OpenSSL development headers for Ubuntu
          sudo apt install -y build-essential 
          sudo apt install python3.11 libpython3.11-dev
          sudo apt install python3.10 libpython3.11-dev
          sudo apt install python3.12
          
      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
        with:
          profile: minimal
          toolchain: nightly

      - name: Cache Rust dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-

      - name: Install MKL
        run: | 
          wget -O- https://apt.repos.intel.com/intel-gpg-keys/GPG-PUB-KEY-INTEL-SW-PRODUCTS.PUB | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/oneapi-archive-keyring.gpg > /dev/null          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/oneapi-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.repos.intel.com/oneapi all main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/oneAPI.list
          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/oneapi-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.repos.intel.com/oneapi all main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/oneAPI.list
          sudo apt update
          sudo apt install -y intel-oneapi-mkl-devel
          export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/2024.2/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"

      - name: Build with Maturin
        run: |
          maturin build --release --out dist --find-interpreter --features mkl,extension-module,ort,audio
      - name: Upload wheels
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wheels-linux-${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          path: dist
  windows:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform.runner }}

    strategy:
      matrix:
        platform:
          # Pinned to VS 2022 (v17): windows-latest moved to Visual Studio 18 (2026),
          # which cmake 0.1.54 (pulled in via aws-lc-sys) can't map to a generator, so
          # the aws-lc-sys CMake build panics with "couldn't determine visual studio generator".
          - runner: windows-2022
            target: x64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.14'
          architecture: ${{ matrix.platform.target }}

      - name: Build wheels
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        env:
          # aws-lc-sys (pulled in transitively via rustls-tls) has no CcBuilder support for
          # x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so it always uses its CMake builder. Feed that build the
          # crate's prebuilt NASM objects so it assembles without a separate NASM install.
          AWS_LC_SYS_PREBUILT_NASM: "1"
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          # Explicit interpreters instead of --find-interpreter: the runner image also ships
          # CPython 3.15, which PyO3 0.25 can't build for (max supported is 3.14).
          args: --release --out dist -i python3.11 python3.12 python3.13 python3.14 --features mkl,extension-module,ort,audio
          sccache: 'true'
      - name: Upload wheels
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wheels-windows-${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          path: dist

  macos:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform.runner }}

    strategy:
      matrix:
        platform:
          - runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: 3.x
      - name: Build wheels
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          args: --release --out dist --find-interpreter --features accelerate,extension-module,ort,audio
          sccache: 'true'
      - name: Upload wheels
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wheels-macos-${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          path: dist

  sdist:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build sdist
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist
      - name: Upload sdist
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wheels-sdist
          path: dist

  release:
    name: Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: "startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')"
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    needs: [linux, windows, macos, sdist]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
      - name: Publish to PyPI
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          command: upload
          args: --non-interactive --skip-existing wheels-*/*",
  "rationale": "The Linux job repeatedly fetches and builds Rust dependencies from crates.io on every run with no cache, while the Windows and macOS jobs already use sccache. The repository has a Cargo.lock that can serve as a cache key. Adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git, keyed by Cargo.lock, reuses downloaded crates across runs without changing build steps, test coverage, or permissions. This matches the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency_cache pattern: it preserves all installation and required tests, uses only GitHub Actions cache infrastructure (no new network endpoints, secrets, or privileged actions), and has no contraindications (no mutable/untrusted cached content, no equivalent cache already present on Linux).",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
